To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in fusion positive tumors, the oncogenic PAX3 FOX01 fusion is driven by a FOXO1 SE that is normally restricted to a late myogenic stage.
a fusion positive rhabdomysarcoma oncogene is driven by a miswired enhancer network that locks rhabdomysosarcoma in a state of undifferentiated myogenesis.

the chief oncogene of fusion positive rhabodomyosarcoma is driven by a super enhancer that is miswired from its normal enhancer network, and that the miswired enhancer network locks the cancer in a state of undifferentiation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of enhancer wiring in the development and maintenance of a cancer.
the logic of enhancer networks and how they are disrupted in cancer.
the logic of enhancer wiring and how enhancers are hijacked by oncogenes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our data reveal a hijacking of enhancer connectivity that disrupts the normal stepwise regulatory logic of skeletal muscle development, replacing it with an infinite loop of enhancer connectivity, locking rhabdomyoblasts in a stage of development that they never leave, thus explaining why these tumors are so difficult to cure.
our study reveals a novel mechanism of oncogene expression and a novel mechanism of enhancer hijacking.

we have identified an enhancer network that is miswired in a cancer of the skeletal muscle lineage and that this enhancer network is responsible for the oncogenic transcription of the fusion gene PAX3 FOX1.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a cancer of the myogenic lineage is driven by enhancer rewiring that disrupts normal CR TF logic.
a fusion oncogene is driven by a hijacked enhancers network that is restricted to a late step of myogenesis.
enhancer miswirings are a common mechanism for cancer development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
enhancer miswirings may be a general mechanism for cancer.
miswired enhancers are a common theme in oncogenesis, and that the enhancer logic in normal development is disrupted in cancer.
miswired enhancer networks can drive oncogenesis.
